solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: a guest who is welcomed in is taken inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a cubic is a mathematical function of the third degree
the lady is referred to as her; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A sweet woman is being received at some social function.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's on lady stands for 'is', so the lady is the thing welcomed into the function.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubic means having the innocent, chubby-cheeked sweetness of a cherub, which is a fair synonym for cute.

indicators.note: something that cuts into a phrase breaks it open and sits inside the gap

parts.note: have to means must
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A demand that the energy cuts be halted.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave to is the sailing term for bringing a vessel to a stop by setting the sails against each other.

clue.text: One way to keep one free

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the road surrounds the numeral

parts.note: a road, abbreviated Rd, is one kind of way
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tip on how to make sure a person stays at liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One way' is a single item, a road, not a one-way street.
explanation.definitionFit: To rid a place of something is to free it from that thing, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: The Queen Vic could be cleaner

definitions.text: The Queen Vic could be cleaner

parts.words: The Queen Vic could be cleaner
parts.note: surface reading: the famous pub could do with a good clean
setter's reading: the Queen Vic is the pub in the TV soap EastEnders, so it is a bar from a soap, and soap cleans

explanation.walkthrough: The Queen Victoria, the Queen Vic, is the pub at the centre of the BBC soap opera EastEnders; a pub is a bar, and a soap's bar is also a cleaning product.
explanation.definitionFit: A cake of soap is used for cleaning, and a pub from a soap opera is a bar belonging to one.

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
on form means playing well

explanation.surface: Supporters follow football clubs that are playing well.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform to rules is to follow or comply with them.

clue.text: Rough pie filled with cold beef

indicators.note: a pie filled with something holds it inside, so one letter goes within the mixed letters
in printing, pie is type that has been jumbled up, so the letters before it are mixed

parts.note: taken as written, to be mixed
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A description of a crude pie stuffed with leftover cold beef.
explanation.walkthrough: Beef looks like part of the filling, but it is the definition, as a verb-turned-noun meaning a complaint; pie is the printer's word for jumbled type.
explanation.definitionFit: A beef is a slang complaint or grievance, and a grouch is likewise a grumble or grudge held against something.

parts.note: in colloquial speech to go is to say, as in 'and he goes, no way'
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A bird is told to speak and show it has understood, as with a parrot.
explanation.walkthrough: Say looks like a homophone signal or 'for example', but it simply gives a casual synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Got it is the everyday expression meaning I have understood, so it stands for understood.

clue.text: Left one under half open window

indicators.note: half means only one of two equal parts is kept, so the back half of the word is lost
in a down clue, being under means placed below, so the earlier pieces come after the halved word

parts.note: taken as written, then halved
port is the left side of a ship
unity is the state of being one

explanation.surface: Someone describes a single item left beneath a partly open window.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' puts the later pieces below the half word.
explanation.definitionFit: A window of opportunity is a short time in which something can be done, so window alone can mean a chance.

clue.text: To seek purification, is inclined to enter church

definitions.note: noun: a cleanse is a purifying regime

indicators.note: something that enters a building ends up inside it, so this phrase sits within the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
leans means is inclined

explanation.surface: A pilgrim seeking spiritual cleansing feels drawn to go into a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the noun: a cleanse, as in a detox or purifying course.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleanse is a course meant to rid the body or spirit of impurities, so it is a purification.

indicators.note: placed around something means surrounding it, so the earlier letters enclose the later word

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
and means together with

explanation.surface: Someone says they will jog about in the company of a vagrant.
explanation.walkthrough: Tramp looks like a noun for a vagrant, but here it is the verb, to walk a long way.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk a long way on foot, and to wander is to roam about on foot without hurry.

parts.note: no tape means nothing to record onto
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone without a recorder is told to put on a record of silence.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'unable to record' is a whimsical description: having NO TAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Not a peep is the idiom for not the slightest sound, which amounts to complete silence.

clue.text: Poor farmer has job covering frozen ground

indicators.note: a cover goes over and around, so the word for a job wraps the mixed letters

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so the word after it is put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be mixed

explanation.surface: A struggling farmer takes on work that involves dealing with frozen land.
explanation.definitionFit: Permafrost is soil that stays below freezing all year round, as in the Arctic tundra.

clue.text: Soldier's breaking concrete like a boss

indicators.note: something breaking into a word splits it and lodges in the gap

parts.note: material as an adjective means physical, concrete
a GI is an American soldier, with the 's attached

explanation.surface: A soldier smashes through concrete with authority.
explanation.walkthrough: Concrete reads as a building material, but it is the adjective meaning physical or real.
explanation.definitionFit: Magisterial means having the authority of a master, commanding and domineering as a boss would be.

parts.note: a ladder in tights is a run, a line of unravelled stitches
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A stepladder is pronounced to be a good one.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a ladder is a run in stockings or tights; the 's means 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rung is one of the crosspieces of a ladder, each one a step to climb on.

parts.note: for good means permanently, always
a measure is an act or action taken, as in a parliamentary measure

explanation.surface: Advice to an actor: always perform as a film extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act as an extra' reads as one phrase about background actors; the split comes after act.
explanation.definitionFit: Something added for good measure is thrown in beyond what is needed, as a bonus or extra.

definitions.note: loosely 'acted as judge of', a past verb like the answer

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters of the next word are twisted

parts.note: taken as written, to be mixed

explanation.surface: A question whether a judge saw a criminal vanish.
explanation.walkthrough: Criminal looks like a noun for the escaping crook, but it is an adjective telling you to mix the next word's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise is to assess or evaluate, so having appraised something is having acted as its judge.

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for avoid is dropped

parts.note: to miss is to avoid
appropriate means right or fitting

explanation.surface: Advice to nearly steer clear of the right-hand pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: Pocket reads as a noun, but it is the verb meaning to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To pocket money dishonestly is to take it for one's own use, which is to misappropriate it.

clue.text: Writer associated with murder and horror describing evil

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw around it, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a mare, short for nightmare, is British slang for a horrible experience
low means base or wicked

explanation.surface: A crime writer known for violent and terrifying tales of wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Marlowe was murdered in a Deptford tavern, and Raymond Chandler's Philip Marlowe investigates murders; either fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlowe is the Elizabethan playwright stabbed to death in 1593, a writer forever linked with killing.

clue.text: About to appear on bloody huge screen

parts.note: re means about, concerning
bloody things are red
OS stands for outsize, huge

explanation.surface: Something is about to be shown on a giant gory cinema screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to appear' reads as 'soon to be shown', but About is the first piece; in a down clue 'on' puts it above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen or partition standing behind a church altar.

clue.text: A policeman at back eating single sweet

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the preceding words are read in reverse
something eating food takes it inside, so a letter goes within the others

parts.note: taken as written
a cop is a policeman
I is the Roman numeral for one, a single
taken as written

explanation.surface: A police officer at the back of a room is eating a single sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At back' tempts as a phrase meaning behind; back actually reverses all of A, the policeman and at.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapioca pudding is a classic British dessert, and sweet is the British word for a dessert course.

indicators.note: to ditch something is to get rid of it, so one letter is thrown out

parts.note: a brief is a set of orders or instructions
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Instructions are given to throw out some good-quality cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Fine looks like praise for the cheese, but it is just the letter to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese with a white rind, named after the region it comes from.

clue.text: Pubs talk English for Gibraltar resident

parts.note: two bars, the plural of pub
to yap is to talk noisily
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Pub chat in English is laid on for a Gibraltarian.
explanation.walkthrough: Pubs gives two bars, one for each letter of the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbary apes are the macaques living wild on the Rock of Gibraltar, its best-known residents.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a light ... of the lips
second meaning: the surname of Basil ..., the fox puppet of British children's TV

explanation.walkthrough: Basil Brush is a puppet fox from long-running British children's television; a fox's tail is also its brush.
explanation.definitionFit: A brush is a light, fleeting touch such as a quick kiss, and it is also the surname that completes Basil's name.

clue.text: On the way out, see kid entering bank

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so the word for kid is placed within the other

parts.note: a mound is a bank of earth
to rib someone is to kid or tease them

explanation.surface: Someone leaving notices a child going into the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: Kid reads as a child, but it is the verb meaning to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Moribund means dying or in terminal decline, so it describes something on its way out.

indicators.note: a letter that opens something splits it apart and sits in the gap

parts.note: a spoon is an old name for a lofted wooden golf club
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: It is the right moment for a nightclub to open its doors.
explanation.walkthrough: Club suggests a nightclub, but the spoon is an old golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is a British informal phrase meaning exactly right or accurate.

indicators.note: the letters are used by, that is contained in, the words that follow

parts.note: found across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A knife blade that tattoo artists work with.
explanation.walkthrough: Blade suggests a cutting edge, but the flat end of a rowing oar is its blade.
explanation.definitionFit: The blade is the flat part of an oar, and rowers commonly call the whole oar a blade.

parts.note: to floor an opponent is to fell or knock them down
ah is what one says on understanding, like I see

explanation.surface: Someone glimpses a farm labourer lying on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: Floor is a verb here, to knock down.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellah is a peasant farmer or agricultural labourer in Egypt and other Arabic-speaking countries.

parts.note: side is an old word for arrogance or swagger, as in putting on side
real means true or genuine

explanation.surface: A remark that conceit is typical of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: Stars suggests celebrities, but here they are in the sky. Side for arrogance is a dated British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal is the astronomical adjective relating to the stars, as in sidereal time measured against them.
